### TASK-275
**Title:** Bounded-room anti-runaway caps for group threads
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** medium
**Spec_References:** specs/OIKONOMOS_GROKBOT_PARITY_REMAINING_WORK_2026-09-16.md ("Bounded-room anti-runaway caps") -- confirmed present in origin/master and merged into CX9's own worktree 2026-09-16T23:10Z (a second real ORCH process gap: re-dispatching a RESUMED builder does not automatically pull new master commits into its existing branch, so the file's earlier commit never actually reached CX9 despite being on master); docs/STUDY-grok-bot-018.md (group chatter cost); services/control-api/src/ports.ts's routeGroupMessage and app.ts's real POST /threads/:id/messages handler (the actual live dispatch/history path)
**Owned_Paths:** services/control-api/src/app.ts, services/control-api/src/ports.ts, services/control-api/src/app.test.ts, packages/db/src/threads.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-274
**Description:** FIRM SCOPE DECISION 2026-09-16T22:35Z, made explicit to prevent a fourth blocked round: CX9 correctly found services/worker has ZERO group-thread awareness anywhere in its production code (confirmed by ORCH: no reference to routeGroupMessage/GroupThread in any non-test worker file). However, tracing the real architecture further shows this does NOT require widening into services/worker/src/main.ts: nothing in this codebase currently makes a bot's own reply automatically trigger a NEW routing round -- every round is only ever initiated by a genuine new inbound message through the real POST /threads/:id/messages endpoint. This means the entire enforcement point is control-api's own routing decision, which can and must check real message history directly (a query against the messages table: count trailing bot-authored messages in the thread, most-recent-first, until hitting a user message) at the exact moment routeGroupMessage runs -- no new state needs to be threaded through task execution or persisted on the run/task rows themselves. The only existing limit on a group thread is the 6-member cap (TASK-180). Nothing bounds how much a group can talk once it starts: no per-round cap, no per-turn message cap, no total-message ceiling, no rule ending a room when nothing new is being said. CONCRETE THRESHOLDS 2026-09-16T23:10Z, per CX9's own correct request that these not be left for the builder to invent: (1) consecutive bot-authored messages cap = 3 -- on the 4th consecutive bot turn since the last user message, routeGroupMessage refuses to auto-route (an explicit @-mention still routes, matching Grok Bot's own documented precedent that a direct mention always overrides chatter limits); (2) rolling history window fed to the Tier-0 scorer = the last 10 messages in the thread, newest-first, truncated there regardless of cap-1's own count; (3) quiet-room threshold = 2 consecutive routed replies whose normalized body text (trim + lowercase, no other fuzzing) is byte-identical to the immediately preceding bot reply in the thread -- on the 2nd repeat, routing stops and a system-authored notice message is inserted into the thread instead of a 3rd bot call. All three numbers are deliberately conservative starting points, not derived from a formula; revisit with real usage data once this ships. Add all three entirely within services/control-api. If CX9 finds a real, concrete counter-example where a bot reply DOES trigger fresh routing without a new inbound message, stop and report it precisely (file:line) rather than assuming this scope decision still holds.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [x] A real group thread cannot produce more than the configured cap of consecutive bot turns without a human message; enforced server-side via evaluateGroupRoomLimits at the routeGroupMessage call site, not on the client.
- [x] A live test proves the cap fires: a real HTTP-route test (app.inject against the actual buildApp routes) confirms a 4th automatic bot turn is refused while an explicit @-mention still routes.
- [x] The "quiet room" detection has a real, live-tested trigger condition: a second HTTP-route test confirms 2 identical trailing bot replies stop routing and insert a real system notice into the thread.
- [x] No regression to TASK-274's single-responder guarantee -- confirmed by direct code read (the new checks run before, not instead of, the existing routing logic) and by the full test suite.

### TASK-279
**Title:** `chat.routes.test.ts`'s TASK-269 continuity test fails deterministically on plain master -- session_ref not seeded on the second turn
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** TBD
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** services/control-api/src/chat.routes.test.ts ("seeds a follow-up message's run with the thread's prior COMPLETED run's session_ref, never on the first message"); TASK-269/270 (the original continuity fix this test protects)
**Owned_Paths:** services/control-api/src/ports.ts, services/control-api/src/chat.routes.test.ts, packages/db/src/runs.ts, packages/db/src/runs.test.ts
**Depends_On:** —
**Description:** Found while reviewing TASK-275 (unrelated to that task's own changes): this specific test fails with `expected null to be 'real-claude-cli-session-abc'` -- the second turn's run is not being seeded with the first turn's captured session_ref, even though the exact same mechanism was verified working multiple times when TASK-269/270 landed. Confirmed by ORCH, independently, twice: reproduces identically on plain master (no TASK-275 changes present) and reproduces identically on TASK-275's own branch -- genuinely pre-existing, not a regression from that task. One candidate lead already ruled out: CX9's own dossier claimed the cause was missing `getThreadEpoch`/`getLatestRunForThread` exports from `packages/db/src/index.ts` -- ORCH confirmed directly that both exports are genuinely present, so that diagnosis does not hold and the real cause is still unknown. Real, live production data is reassuring but not conclusive: maximus's real runs (currently Gemini-provider) show the same session_ref correctly carrying across 5 consecutive real turns -- but Gemini's own continuity mechanism (buildGeminiTurnPrompt reconstructing full history) does not depend on session_ref seeding the way the Claude lane does, so this may not actually exercise the same code path the failing test protects. The Claude lane cannot currently be live-tested at all (Anthropic account has been out of credit since earlier this session) -- this is exactly the kind of gap that could be silently broken for real Claude-provider bots specifically, with no way to notice until credits are restored, which is why this is filed at high priority rather than dismissed as test-only noise.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [x] Real root cause identified with direct evidence: a genuine polling race in the TEST ITSELF, not a logic bug. `submitTaskExecution` (app.ts's `void submit.catch(...)`, deliberately fire-and-forget) creates the run row and THEN, in the same async chain, conditionally calls `resumeRun` to seed `session_ref` before enqueueing. `waitForRunOtherThan`'s poll could observe the row in the window between row creation and `resumeRun` landing. Confirmed by direct reproduction: getThreadEpoch/getLatestRunForThread/resumeRun/completeRun all returned exactly the expected values every time when called directly against the isolated DB outside the test harness -- the continuity logic itself was never broken.
- [x] Fix applied and the specific test passes reliably: debounced the poll to only accept a row once two reads 25ms apart agree on both status and session_ref. Verified with two consecutive full isolated-suite runs, 295/295 both times.
- [ ] A genuine live test on the Claude lane specifically, once Anthropic credit is restored -- still open, correctly left unticked; nothing found here changes that the Claude lane itself remains unverifiable live until billing is restored.
- [x] Full recursive suite green after the fix: 23/23 files, 295/295 tests, twice.

### TASK-281
**Title:** Template install/export completeness -- copy skills, create paused/unbudgeted routines, and opt-in memory copy (ADR-018 §3/§5)
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** docs/decisions/ADR-018-bot-templates.md §3 ("It then copies skills, creates routines paused and unbudgeted, writes opt-in profile memories"), §5 ("Routines travel paused and unbudgeted; memories travel only by explicit opt-in"); specs/OIKONOMOS_TEMPLATES_v1.0.md §5.2
**Owned_Paths:** services/control-api/src/templates.ts, services/control-api/src/templates.test.ts, services/control-api/src/ports.ts, services/control-api/package.json
**Depends_On:** TASK-278
**Description:** Found during TASK-278's own review: the merged export/install routes satisfy ADR-018 §2 (credential scan) and §3's grant-boundary requirement (built-in floor only, no template-derived grant), but do NOT implement the rest of §3's own explicit text. Confirmed directly by reading the merged code: (1) export hardcodes `integrations: []` and `memories: []` unconditionally -- the route already accepts an `include_memories?: string[]` body field but it is dead, never read (`services/control-api/src/templates.ts` line ~102, comment reads "Memory is opt-in and has no control-api port in this task's scope"); (2) install creates the role, the grant floor, and the provenance row, but never calls `createSkill`/`setEnabledForRole` for the manifest's skills, never calls `createRoutine` for the manifest's routines, and never writes any memory fact -- so an installed bot today has zero skills, zero routines, and zero memory regardless of what the exported template contained. `@oikonomos/memory` (packages/memory/src/facts.ts: `readProfileTier`, `writeMemoryFact`) is not yet a dependency of services/control-api at all -- confirmed via grep, needs adding to package.json and wiring into ports.ts, the same class of gap TASK-278 hit repeatedly with `@oikonomos/templates`. `createSkill`, `setEnabledForRole`, `createRoutine`, `setRoutinePaused` are ALL already wired into ports.ts (confirmed by grep) -- only the memory port is missing, everything else is a templates.ts wiring task.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [x] Export reads the role's real integrations from its actual grants (join role_grants -> capabilities) and populates `integrations[]` with each capability_id and its current maxTier, not an empty array.
- [x] Export reads memory facts ONLY for keys explicitly named in `include_memories` (default: absent/empty = no memories exported, matching ADR-018 §5's "the default selection is none"), via `readProfileTier`, agent-scope profile-tier facts only.

### TASK-292
**Title:** clawsrv OpenSandbox host-port exhaustion -- live sandbox creation failing at ~65% rate
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** TBD

**Description:** While reviewing TASK-289, the full recursive suite showed 3 unrelated failures (sandbox-client, evals/harness, worker), all `SandboxClientError: OpenSandbox create-sandbox returned unexpected status 500 (DOCKER::SANDBOX_START_FAILED)`. Traced directly on clawsrv: `docker logs opensandbox-server --since 60m` shows repeated `driver failed programming external connectivity ... Bind for 0.0.0.0:3xxxx failed: port is already allocated` on sandbox/egress-sidecar container start -- 19 HTTP 500s vs 10 HTTP 202s on `POST /v1/sandboxes` in the last hour (~65% failure rate). `docker ps --filter name=sandbox-egress` shows 97 currently-running egress sidecar containers -- almost certainly accumulated, leaked sandboxes (never destroyed after their run/test finished) exhausting the host's ephemeral port range and causing new sandbox creates to collide. This is a LIVE production defect: real chat runs requiring a sandbox are failing at this same rate right now, not just tests. Likely related to TASK-231's already-documented "conservative cleanup, does not eliminate all fixture/orphan pollution" finding, now compounded to production-impacting scale. Deliberately NOT touched directly during this review -- killing/pruning 97 containers on shared production infra without first distinguishing genuinely-active sandboxes from leaked ones is a real, hard-to-reverse action; needs the user's go-ahead (or a careful audit script that checks each container's actual owning run/task state before removal) rather than a unilateral bulk docker prune.

- [ ] (MOVED to TASK-296) A real cleanup mechanism (either fixed at the source, or a periodic reaper keyed on genuine run/task state, never on container age alone) that returns clawsrv to a low steady-state sandbox count.
- [x] Live proof: `POST /v1/sandboxes` success rate back to ~100% over a sustained window, not just immediately after a one-time manual cleanup.
- [ ] (MOVED to TASK-296) A liveness assertion per CLAUDE.md's "every mechanical control ships a liveness assertion" rule -- this failure mode must be detectable going forward, not just fixed once.

### TASK-293
**Title:** template-status false drift on freshly installed roles -- compare against an install-time baseline, not the raw template manifest
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** S5
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** specs/OIKONOMOS_TEMPLATES_v1.0.md §6.1 (drift = role changed since install), §6.2 ("Drift is shown, never auto-synced"); §5 install semantics (name override, opt-in `include_memories`, reuse of same-named tenant skills, integrations surfaced as a grant checklist rather than auto-granted).
**Owned_Paths:** infra/postgres/migrations/029_role_template_install_baseline.up.sql, infra/postgres/migrations/029_role_template_install_baseline.down.sql, packages/db/src/templates.ts, packages/db/src/templates.test.ts, services/control-api/src/templates.ts, services/control-api/src/templates.test.ts, services/control-api/src/ports.ts, packages/templates/src/migration.test.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-289
**Description:** Found by ORCH's independent review of TASK-289 (the old ORCH session merged it before that review completed). The shipped route compares the role's live projection against the *template version's* manifest, but install intentionally does not reproduce that manifest exactly, so a role installed a second ago with zero edits reports `drift: true` whenever: (1) it was installed with a `name` override -> `identity`; (2) the template carries memories the installer did not opt into via `include_memories` -> `memories` (status builds memoryKeys from the template, the role holds fewer); (3) install reused an existing same-named tenant skill whose body differs -> `skills`; (4) template integrations beyond the default floor are only surfaced in the grant checklist, not granted -> `integrations` until the human grants them. TASK-289's real-Postgres test used a bare role and structurally cannot hit any of these. Fix: at install, after all install writes complete, project the newly created role with the same `projectCurrentManifest` helper and persist that as the install's baseline (new nullable `baseline_manifest jsonb` column on `role_template_installs` via migration 029, written in the same install flow; keep rows immutable). Status compares live projection vs baseline per section, using the baseline's memory keys. Legacy install rows with a null baseline fall back to the existing template-manifest compare (documented in a code comment); do not add response fields -- the shape is fixed for TASK-291. Case (4) judgement: granting a checklist integration after install IS a real change to the role and should report `integrations` drift -- that's correct behaviour, test it as such. Response shape must not change (TASK-291 consumes it in parallel).
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] Real Postgres test: install with a `name` override, no edits -> `drift: false, changed: []`.
- [ ] Real Postgres test: template with >=1 memory, installed without opting in -> `drift: false`.
- [ ] Real Postgres test: template with a skill whose name matches an existing tenant skill with a different body -> `drift: false` immediately after install.
- [ ] Real Postgres test: template requesting an integration beyond the default floor -> `drift: false` right after install; after granting it -> `drift: true, changed: ["integrations"]`.
- [ ] Existing TASK-289 cases (never installed / unchanged / instructions edited) still pass.
- [ ] Migration 029 up and down both apply cleanly; register-capabilities/test-isolated -Init re-run if the harness requires it.
- [ ] Full recursive suite via `scripts/test-isolated.ps1` only (never a direct DATABASE_URL run -- production spend risk, see 2026-09-15 incident). Pre-existing sandbox failures caused by TASK-292's live port exhaustion must be named as such in Test_Evidence, not hidden.

### TASK-294
**Title:** CAN-03 banned-modes eval: flaky 5s timeout, and no liveness assertion in the eval itself
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** medium
**Spec_References:** docs/decisions/ADR-002-permission-bypass-ban-scope.md §4 + Amendment A; docs/decisions/ADR-005-control-liveness.md ("every mechanical control ships a liveness assertion ... keyed on evidence the control emits by doing its job").
**Owned_Paths:** evals/harness/test/can-03-banned-modes.test.ts
**Depends_On:** —
**Description:** Found by ORCH investigation 2026-09-17, triggered by a real intermittent failure in TASK-289's full-suite run ("can-03 ... hit the 5000ms timeout while starting the scanner as a child process"). Verified directly: the test is NOT inert and the scanner is NOT broken -- `node infra/ci/banned-modes.mjs` walks 1223 files, 0 violations, 12 allowlist entries, and planting a token makes it exit 1. The real defects are: (1) the test spawns a whole-repo scan that takes ~4.85s against vitest's 5000ms default -- it will flake more often as the repo grows, and a control that intermittently fails for timing reasons trains reviewers to ignore it; (2) can-03's body is three assertions on a clean run only, so the eval alone cannot distinguish a live scanner from one that trivially prints "banned-modes: clean". The genuine positive control exists but lives in a different suite (infra/ci/test-banned-modes.mjs, node:test), which is not the suite a reviewer runs as the CAN gate. Fix both in the eval: give it an explicit generous timeout, and add a planted-violation case (temp file under an enforcement surface, asserting a non-zero exit and a hit count, cleaned up afterwards) so the eval fails when the scanner goes inert. Do not weaken or widen the ADR-002 allowlist; infra/ci/** is a protected path and is deliberately NOT in this task's Owned_Paths.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [x] can-03 has an explicit timeout comfortably above the observed whole-repo scan time, with a comment naming the measured duration and why.
- [x] can-03 contains a positive control: a planted banned token on an enforcement surface makes the scanner exit non-zero and the assertion proves it, with guaranteed cleanup even on failure.
- [x] The negative (clean-repo) assertion is retained; a scanner that rejected everything must still fail the eval.
- [x] No change to infra/ci/** and no allowlist widening.
- [x] evals/harness suite green.
**Branch:** task/TASK-294-cx9
**Started_At:** 2026-09-17T22:17:03Z
**Progress_Notes:**
- [2026-09-17T22:35:00Z] [ORCH] Filed from a direct investigation (scanner exercised live, both directions). Not a hypothetical: the flake already cost real signal in TASK-289's review.
**Artifacts:** can-03 30s timeout + planted-violation positive control (commit 56f511d, merged)
**Test_Evidence:** ORCH independent run in wt-codex9, isolated harness only: CAN-03 passed 5/5 consecutive runs (1.2-9.8s). Confirmed temp .can-03-* dirs cleaned up after every run (finally block works). Confirmed the positive control is non-vacuous: infra/ci/lib/walk.mjs skips directories only by exact basename (.git/.turbo/.pnpm-store/node_modules/dist/coverage/.devteam), no dotfile convention, so the planted violation under evals/** is genuinely scanned and caught. The one recurring harness-suite failure (ome-two-role-handoff-live.test.ts, live Gemini/sandbox infra) is unrelated and present in every run.
**Review_Findings:** Approved first-pass. Territory clean (1 owned file + own dossier). Token assembled at runtime (["bypass","Permissions"].join("")) so the test file does not self-trip the scanner it is testing -- matches the scanner's own pattern. No infra/ci/** touched, no allowlist widening.

### TASK-295
**Title:** Banned-modes scanner misses non-Claude permission-bypass vocabulary (`codex exec -s danger-full-access`)
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** S5
**Priority:** medium
**Spec_References:** docs/decisions/ADR-002-permission-bypass-ban-scope.md Amendment B, "Second finding" + "Residual risk (d)": "CX's invocation is `codex exec -s danger-full-access`. That is functionally equivalent permission bypass, but it is not one of the three tokens CAN-03 greps for ... CAN-03's token list tracks the Claude Code vocabulary and does not generalise across CLIs" and "(d) The CAN-03 token-list gap for non-Claude CLIs is not closed by this amendment and remains open -- a future change should either generalise the grep or record why it need not be."
**Owned_Paths:** infra/ci/banned-modes.mjs, infra/ci/test-banned-modes.mjs, infra/ci/lib/allowlist.mjs, infra/ci/banned-modes-allowlist.txt, packages/agent-providers/test/providers.grok.test.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-294
**Description:** DECIDED 2026-09-19 (owner: "continue with your recommendation"; Grok is not currently a builder, so the adversarial reviewer is CX9, the only non-Claude model available). S5's work (task/TASK-295-s5, commit 2c0ec0e) widened the scanner to the Codex flag+value forms and correctly stopped on two items. ORCH resolutions: (A) `.codex/config.toml` must NOT be blanket-exempted. ORCH read it: line 21 is a comment, but line 23 (`sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`) and line 35 (the `[profiles.builder]` copy) are LIVE permission settings. ADR-002 says config-bearing surfaces are scanned with no exceptions (`.claude/settings*.json` is the precedent), and a `.codex/**` carve-out would hide the exact class this task exists to catch. Also, S5's flag+value tokens (`-s danger-full-access`) do not match the TOML key form, so the branch scanner currently misses the live config lines entirely. Do this instead: (1) add the TOML key form (`sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`, tolerant of whitespace and quote style) as a banned form; (2) add `.codex/**` to ENFORCEMENT_SURFACES in infra/ci/lib/allowlist.mjs (config-bearing, mirrors `.claude/settings*.json`); (3) add a NEW token-scoped, count-pinned exemption mechanism: an exemption is keyed on (exact file, exact token) with an exact expected hit count, lives in code (not the free-text allowlist file, whose header says its lines cannot override enforcement surfaces), and FAILS when the actual count differs in EITHER direction, so growth is rejected and a removed occurrence forces the pin down instead of going stale. Register exactly the currently-true Codex danger-full-access occurrences in `.codex/config.toml` (measure them; do not trust the line numbers above), justified by ADR-002 Amendment B (owner Option D: the territory pre-commit hook is the compensating control). (B) Grok `--always-approve`: add it to the banned tokens with ONE pinned exemption for `packages/agent-providers/src/providers/grok.ts` (measure the real count; at least the comment on line 15 and the push on line 55), justified by ADR-011 (reviewed, broker-gated product provider). Grok is not a builder now, but the token concerns enforcement surfaces regardless of the builder roster, and adding it now means reactivating GB later cannot silently reopen the gap. Replace S5's test asserting the token is ABSENT with tests asserting it is present. Everything else stands: scripts/** and autopilot.json stay carved out per ADR-002 2(2); do not weaken existing tests; infra/ci/** is a protected path. The reviewer must explicitly assess that the .codex pin cannot be widened without failing CI, because CX9's own invocation vocabulary is the subject. ORIGINAL SCOPE (2026-09-17): ADR-002 itself left this open in August 2026 and it is still open. CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #2 bans permission bypass platform-wide "including all subagents", but the mechanical scanner only knows three Claude Code tokens. CX9 (a Codex unit) is dispatched routinely, so the ungoverned vocabulary is in live use by a real builder, not theoretical. Generalise the token list to cover the equivalent bypass vocabulary of every CLI in autopilot.json's registry (at minimum Codex's `-s danger-full-access` / `--sandbox danger-full-access` and `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`; check the current Codex CLI surface rather than trusting this list, and check Grok Build's equivalent too). Keep the ADR-002 enforcement-surface/prose-surface split exactly as it is -- scripts/** and autopilot.json remain carved out per §2(2), which is precisely why dispatch.ps1 legitimately carries these flags today. **infra/ci/** is a PROTECTED PATH: this task requires adversarial review by a different model than the author (Codex CLI per CLAUDE.md), so do not assign it to CX9, whose own invocation vocabulary it governs.
**Acceptance_Criteria:** 
- [ ] The scanner detects the Codex bypass vocabulary in all three forms: the CLI flag (`-s` / `--sandbox danger-full-access`), `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, and the config-file key form (`sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`); each has a planted-token test in both directions. (ADR-002 Amendment B, residual risk (d))
- [ ] `.codex/**` is an enforcement surface; `.codex/config.toml`'s live occurrences are covered by a token-scoped exemption pinned to the exact current count; a planted extra occurrence (a new profile) fails, and lowering the real count without lowering the pin also fails.
- [ ] `--always-approve` is a banned token; exactly one pinned exemption exists (grok.ts); the token planted in any other file (a sibling provider, a .github workflow) fails; a third occurrence in grok.ts fails; a bare CodexSandbox enum value in packages/agent-providers (no flag) is still not flagged.
- [ ] The current repo passes clean, scripts/** and autopilot.json remain carved out, and existing tests pass unmodified apart from the replaced Grok-absence pin.
- [ ] The mechanism, both exemptions and the residual (a genuine bypass added inside an exempted file is caught only through the count change) are documented in-file with pointers to ADR-002 Amendment B (d) and ADR-011; the dossier supplies the ADR-002 Amendment C text for ORCH to write (builders never own docs/**).
- [ ] Adversarial review by CX9 (non-Claude) recorded in REVIEW.md, explicitly covering the pin mechanism.

### TASK-296
**Title:** Sandbox office lifecycle -- reap orphaned/idle offices, request a server-side TTL, pause the Gemini lane, alert on leak growth
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** S5
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** docs/decisions/ADR-010-persistent-office-computer-pivot.md (a persistent per-role office is INTENDED -- do not destroy after every run); docs/decisions/ADR-005-control-liveness.md (every mechanical control ships a liveness assertion keyed on evidence the control emits by doing its job); infra/sandbox/README.md:120 (server-side TTL reaping verified working).
**Owned_Paths:** services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.ts, services/worker/src/sandboxReaper.ts, services/worker/src/sandboxReaper.test.ts, services/worker/src/main.ts, packages/sandbox-client/src/client.ts, packages/sandbox-client/src/types.ts, packages/db/src/roleSandboxes.ts, packages/db/src/roleSandboxes.test.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-292
**Description:** Closes the CODE half of the TASK-292 incident; the live cleanup is already done and verified (see TASK-292 notes for the measured root cause). Four defects, in priority order. (1) ORPHAN/IDLE REAPER: `role_sandboxes.last_used_at` exists and is indexed (018_role_sandboxes.up.sql) and nothing reads it. Add a reaper that destroys an office whose role no longer exists, or whose `last_used_at` is older than a configurable idle window. Key it on genuine role/run state, NEVER on container age alone -- an old office in daily use must survive, a fresh office for a deleted fixture role must not. It must also handle the orphan class with no DB row at all (offices whose role row was cascade-deleted by scripts/db-cleanup.mjs) by reconciling the server's own sandbox list against live roles; `metadata.roleId` is already set at creation, so the mapping exists. (2) TTL: pass `timeout` on createSandbox so the server's own reaper is a backstop when our process dies mid-turn; pick a window that cannot kill a legitimately in-use office and justify the number in a comment. (3) RELEASE ON FAILURE: the Claude lane's pause sits after a throw (chatRunDriver.ts:884-889) and the Gemini lane (chatRunDriver.ts:704) never pauses at all -- move the pause into a `finally` in BOTH lanes. (4) LIVENESS + ALERT: the control must fail when it is inert. Key it on evidence the reaper emits by doing its job (a sweep record/metric with counts), plus a threshold assertion on live office or held-port count. Never key it on configuration being present.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [x] Reaper destroys an office whose role no longer exists, and one idle beyond the window; tests prove BOTH directions (an old-but-actively-used office is NOT reaped).
- [x] Reaper reconciles server-side sandboxes that have no DB row (cascade-deleted fixture roles) via metadata.roleId; a test covers that class specifically.
- [x] Every createSandbox passes a non-zero `timeout`; a test asserts it, and a comment justifies the window.
- [x] Both Claude and Gemini lanes pause the office in a `finally`; a test where the turn throws proves the office is still released.
- [x] A liveness assertion that fails when the reaper is inert, keyed on emitted sweep evidence rather than configuration.
- [x] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only, never a direct DATABASE_URL (2026-09-15 production-spend incident).

### TASK-297
**Title:** scripts/test-isolated.ps1 hangs indefinitely on a wedged Task Scheduler query
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** medium
**Spec_References:** none (tooling defect found during TASK-292 verification).
**Owned_Paths:** scripts/test-isolated.ps1
**Depends_On:** —
**Description:** Found 2026-09-18 while verifying TASK-292. scripts/test-isolated.ps1:93 queries the OIKONOMOS-ServiceWatchdog scheduled task; Task Scheduler on this workstation is currently wedged -- both `schtasks /Query` and `Get-ScheduledTask` hang indefinitely (>60s standalone) although the Schedule service reports Running. The harness therefore sat ~15 minutes with zero output, no timeout, no error and no fallback; killing the stuck schtasks.exe child let the suite run normally. Because this harness is the ONLY sanctioned way to run tests (a direct DATABASE_URL run is a real production-spend risk per the 2026-09-15 incident), a silent indefinite hang here blocks all verification and invites exactly the shortcut that caused that incident. Fix: bound the query and degrade loudly -- if watchdog state cannot be determined, either proceed with it treated as not-ready or abort with a clear message, never hang. The wedged Task Scheduler itself likely needs a Schedule service restart or a reboot; that is a machine-level action for the user, not part of this task.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [x] The scheduled-task query cannot hang the script: bounded wait, with the timeout value and reasoning in a comment.
- [x] On timeout the script emits an unmissable message and takes a defined path (proceed-degraded or abort), never a silent indefinite wait.
- [x] Existing watchdog disable/restore behaviour is unchanged when the query succeeds, including the finally-block restore.
- [x] Verified by simulating a hanging query (injected stub), not by reasoning alone.

**Title:** Atomic budget reservation protocol for the project and role axes -- database layer (P-3a)
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** S5
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** specs/OIKONOMOS_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_v1.0.md §6.2 (the full reservation protocol: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE ledger rows, recorded spend + open reservations per axis, deny before spawn, release exactly once), §11 (two simultaneous near-limit admissions -> at most one admitted); docs/decisions/ADR-019-project-entity-and-manager-role.md §5 'Atomic admission' steps 1-4.
**Owned_Paths:** packages/db/src/spendReservations.ts, packages/db/src/spendReservations.test.ts, packages/db/src/spend.ts, packages/db/src/spend.test.ts, packages/db/src/index.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-298
**Description:** Pure database layer, no worker wiring (TASK-301 wires it). Implement `admitRunReservation({tenantId, runId, projectId|null, roleId, reserveUsd, month})` as ONE transaction: upsert-then-`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` the budget_ledgers rows for the run's project axis and role axis (only the axes that apply -- a run with no project only checks the role axis, and a role with budget_usd NULL has no role ceiling); for each axis compute this month's recorded spend_records + open (released_at IS NULL) reservations; if adding reserveUsd would exceed the ceiling, roll back and return a typed denial naming the axis (`budget.project_exceeded` / `budget.role_exceeded`); else insert one spend_reservations row per applicable axis and commit, returning the reservation ids. `releaseRunReservation(runId)` sets released_at exactly once (guarded `WHERE released_at IS NULL`, returns whether it released). Extend the spend-record insert in spend.ts so recording spend for a run releases that run's open reservations IN THE SAME TRANSACTION as the spend_records insert (ADR-019 §5 step 3). Currency: ADR-019 specifies USD columns while the platform ceiling is ZAR -- keep this layer in USD exactly as the ADR says; do not convert here.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] Two concurrent near-limit admissions on the same project axis: exactly one succeeds and the other is denied budget.project_exceeded -- proven with two genuinely concurrent real-Postgres transactions, not sequential calls. (spec §6.2, §11)
- [ ] The same concurrency proof on the role axis with budget.role_exceeded. (spec §6.2, §11)
- [ ] Open reservations count against the ceiling alongside recorded spend. (spec §6.2)
- [ ] A reservation is released exactly once: releasing twice is a no-op, and recording spend releases it in the same transaction as the spend_records insert (a test proves a failed insert leaves the reservation open). (spec §6.2)
- [ ] A role with budget_usd NULL and a run with no project are admitted without touching those axes. (spec §6.2)
- [ ] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only.

### TASK-301
**Title:** Wire atomic admission into both chat lanes and the subprocess path; attribute spend to project and role (P-3b)
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** specs/OIKONOMOS_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_v1.0.md §6.1 (every run started from a project thread or a task.assigned handoff is attributed to the project), §6.2 (deny before spawn; release on failure), §6.3 (manager budget covers only its own turns), §11; docs/decisions/ADR-019-project-entity-and-manager-role.md §5.
**Owned_Paths:** packages/broker/src/budgetGate.ts, packages/broker/src/budgetGate.test.ts, services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.ts, services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.test.ts, services/worker/src/subprocessProviders.ts, services/worker/src/roleMessageDelivery.ts, services/worker/src/executeRun.ts, services/worker/test/executeRun.test.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-300, TASK-299, TASK-311, TASK-315, TASK-316, TASK-318
**Description:** PROTECTED PATH (packages/broker/**): adversarial review by a model different from the author is mandatory. Add `budget.project_exceeded` and `budget.role_exceeded` to budgetGate's deny vocabulary (the pure gate keeps evaluating platform/provider/routine first, unchanged -- spec 6.2). Call TASK-300's admitRunReservation BEFORE any provider spawn in: the Claude sandbox lane, the Gemini lane (chatRunDriver.ts, where assertChatBudgetAllows runs today at :416), and services/worker/src/subprocessProviders.ts. On a denial, fail the run before spawn with the axis-specific reason. On a run that fails before any spend is recorded, release the reservation on the existing failure path (noteFailureUnrecordedSpend / noteUnrecordedSpend, chatRunDriver.ts ~:307/:409/:520/:1311). Attribution: a run is attributed to a project when its thread is a project's thread (getProjectByThreadId) OR it was created by roleMessageDelivery.ts from a task.assigned handoff (read project_id from the locator TASK-299 adds). AUTHORIZATION (found in ORCH's review of TASK-299): any bot can send the typed project kinds through send_to_role, and TASK-299 can only check thread membership, not the manager flag. So attribute a delivered handoff to a project ONLY when its sender is that project's manager (project_roles.is_manager, TASK-298) and its recipient is on the roster; otherwise deliver it as an ordinary handoff with no project attribution and no project reservation. Without this, a forged task.assigned could burn another project's budget. Reservation size: ADR-019 says 'the provider's documented per-turn maximum, the same ceiling TASK-220 uses', but NO such constant exists in the codebase (verified: only GEMINI_CAP_MISSING_REASON in geminiChatRun.ts). Define one explicit, named, env-overridable per-turn reservation per provider in this task, justify each number in a comment against the real provider cost calculators in packages/agent-providers, and never let an unset value mean 'no reservation'.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] No provider is invoked when either axis would be exceeded: two simultaneous near-limit runs on the same project produce at most one provider invocation, the other denied budget.project_exceeded before spawn -- proven through the real run path with a counting fake provider. (spec §11)
- [ ] Same proof on the role axis with budget.role_exceeded. (spec §11)
- [ ] A task.assigned handoff whose sender is not the project's manager, or whose recipient is not on the roster, produces NO project attribution and reserves nothing against the project (proven with a forged handoff). (ORCH review of TASK-299)
- [ ] A run from a project thread, and a run delivered from a manager's task.assigned handoff, both write spend_records.project_id; a manager's own turns are charged to the manager role, a specialist's to the specialist and the project, never to the manager. (spec §6.1, §6.3)
- [ ] A run that fails before spend releases its reservation exactly once. (spec §6.2)
- [ ] Platform, provider and routine gate behaviour unchanged; existing budget tests pass unmodified. (spec §6.2)
- [ ] Adversarial review by a different model than the author recorded in REVIEW.md.
- [ ] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only.

**Depends_On:** TASK-298, TASK-302
**Description:** Mirror templates.ts: a registerProjectRoutes(app, deps) registrar in projects.ts called once from app.ts (the templates call is at app.ts:1103), ports added to ControlApiDeps in ports.ts. POST /projects creates the group thread through the SAME code path POST /threads/group uses (app.ts:1521 -- reuse, do not duplicate), writes projects + project_roles + thread_members in one transaction, caps the roster at 6, allows at most one manager, and writes the charter (goal, done criterion, boundaries, 'check with me before') as scope='project' tier='profile' facts via @oikonomos/memory writeMemoryFact. If a manager is chosen, grant that role the six ENABLED project.* capabilities AND workspace.create_bot ONLY (workspace.retire_bot is NOT granted in v1: TASK-310 review, scoped by TASK-313) (human-initiated via this route, same grant port the existing grant route uses; ADR-019 Amendment 2026-09-19: managers create and retire bots through the existing approval-gated workspace tools) -- never project.request_grant (declared disabled) and never any capability that writes grants. When a role stops being a manager (PATCH /projects/:id), ONE transaction must (a) revoke those grants and (b) invalidate every pending workspace.create_bot approval issued to that role. TASK-310 finding 3: approvals bind only the action digest and a nonce, not manager state, so a stale pending approval would otherwise stay human-grantable after demotion. Use the existing approvals invalidation primitives (packages/approvals is a protected path: if none fits, stop with OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT naming the function needed rather than editing it). Prove it: create a pending create_bot approval, demote, and a consume attempt must fail. Every route is tenant-scoped via findTenantOwnedThread (app.ts:694), 404 never 403. Approvals decided on any run attributed to the project are mirrored into project_decisions by approval_id reference in the decideApproval port (ports.ts ~:691), never by copying the render. Add blockedTasks per project thread to db/workspaceSummary.ts. D1 project directory: there is no server-side mkdir for D1 (it lives in the sandbox; ensureSandboxWorkspace creates dirs at run time) -- RESOLVED by ORCH: the directory is created lazily by the first writer; the route does not create it, and register_artifact (TASK-302) validates the prefix. Visibility of the charter to member runs depends on TASK-306 (memory injection); this task only proves the facts are written with the right scope.

### TASK-311
**Title:** Sandbox office lifecycle defect: a role whose recorded sandbox is gone (or Terminated/Failed) fails every turn forever -- recreate it
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** S5
**Priority:** critical
**Spec_References:** docs/decisions/ADR-010-persistent-office-computer-pivot.md (persistent per-role office; a removed office costs only a cold start); TASK-296 (merged; this fixes a defect found on its deployment); services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.ts resolveRoleSandbox and its own comment "a genuinely dead sandbox ... must still fail closed".
**Owned_Paths:** services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.ts, services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.test.ts, services/worker/src/sandboxReaper.ts, services/worker/src/sandboxReaper.test.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-296
**Description:** PRODUCTION INCIDENT 2026-09-19, found while deploying TASK-296. `resolveRoleSandbox` creates an office only when `role_sandboxes` has NO record. When a record exists and the server no longer has that sandbox, `client.getSandbox()` throws (404) and the turn fails; when the record says Terminated/Failed, `waitForSandboxRunning` throws. Nothing ever recreates it. Consequences observed: (1) after ORCH's TASK-292 cleanup on 2026-09-18 removed every leaked office, the two real bots (maximus, jipolt) had records still saying Running for destroyed sandboxes, so every chat turn for them would have failed; ORCH repaired it by hand by deleting the two stale rows. ORCH had wrongly stated earlier that the code recovers by design. (2) TASK-296's idle-reaper marks a reaped, still-active role's office Terminated on the assumption that the next turn recreates it (see the comment in sandboxReaper.ts), so the reaper as merged can strand a role permanently. TASK-296's test never ran a turn after a reap, which is why review missed it. FIX: in resolveRoleSandbox, treat a 404 from getSandbox, and a Terminated or Failed live state, as "the office is gone": create a fresh sandbox exactly as the no-record path does (same image, entrypoint, limits, egress policy, TTL timeout) and overwrite the role record with the new sandbox id (upsertRoleSandbox already overwrites by role). Any OTHER getSandbox error (unreachable server, 5xx, auth) must still fail closed -- never create a duplicate office because the server was briefly unreachable. Make the reaper and resolveRoleSandbox agree: after an idle reap the next turn must succeed. Guard against two concurrent turns for one role creating two sandboxes after a 404 (say in a comment which existing per-role serialisation prevents it, with evidence, or add one).
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] A role whose record points at a sandbox that returns 404 gets a fresh office on its next turn, the record is overwritten with the new id, and the turn succeeds -- proven for both the Claude and Gemini lanes.
- [ ] The same for a record whose live state is Terminated or Failed.
- [ ] A non-404 getSandbox failure (network error, 500, 401) still fails the turn closed and creates nothing.
- [ ] End-to-end regression test: reap an idle active role's office with the real reaper, then run a turn for that role through resolveRoleSandbox against real Postgres -- the turn succeeds with a new office. (This is the test TASK-296 lacked.)
- [ ] Two concurrent turns for one role after a 404 never leave two live sandboxes, proven by test or by cited existing serialisation.
- [ ] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only; failures classified against the master baseline.
- [ ] Reviewed by Opus 5 or another model that is NOT claude-sonnet-5 (the author), recorded in REVIEW.md.
**Branch:** task/TASK-311-s5
**Started_At:** 2026-09-19T07:44:07Z

Needs non-Sonnet-5 review.

Territory clean (chatRunDriver.ts + sandboxReaper.test.ts + own dossier, all in Owned_Paths). ### TASK-315
**Title:** Role budget axis reads zero for real spend -- derive a role's recorded spend from run -> task -> role, not from spend_records.routine_id
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** S5
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** specs/OIKONOMOS_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_v1.0.md §6.2 (per-role ceiling, `budget.role_exceeded`), §6.3 (a manager's own turns are charged to the manager, a specialist's to the specialist), §11 (role-axis concurrent admission); docs/decisions/ADR-019-project-entity-and-manager-role.md §5; docs/decisions/ADR-005-control-liveness.md (a control must fail when inert).
**Owned_Paths:** packages/db/src/spendReservations.ts, packages/db/src/spendReservations.test.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-300
**Description:** Found by ORCH after TASK-300 merged (54e598d); autopilot's review approved it without catching this. `admitRunReservation` computes a role's recorded spend as `SUM(cost_usd) FROM spend_records WHERE routine_id = <roleId>` (spendReservations.ts header and the `spendColumn` line: "spend_records has no role column; attribution wiring is TASK-301"). But every real chat run records spend with `routineId: request.task.routineId` (chatRunDriver.ts:858 and :1323), which is NULL for a plain chat and the routine's own id for a routine run -- never the role id. So the role axis sums to ZERO for all real spend and `budget.role_exceeded` can never fire: a spending ceiling that looks live and does nothing. "TASK-301 will attribute accordingly" is not a fix: recording the role id in routine_id would destroy per-routine attribution, which the routine budget gate reads. FIX, no schema change: a role's recorded spend for the month is the sum over spend_records joined through the run to its task's role: `spend_records s JOIN runs r ON r.run_id::text = s.run_id JOIN tasks t ON t.task_id = r.task_id WHERE t.role_id = $roleId` (spend_records.run_id is text, runs.run_id and tasks.task_id are uuid, tasks.role_id is text; join on `r.run_id::text = s.run_id` so a non-UUID run id can never raise a cast error). That charges every run of the role, chat and routine alike, and leaves routine_id alone. Keep the project axis (spend_records.project_id) and the reservation and release logic unchanged. The tests must be able to FAIL against the merged code, which is what TASK-300's tests could not do.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] Recorded spend for a role is derived through run -> task -> role; spend recorded by a plain chat run (routine_id NULL) counts against that role's ceiling, and so does a routine run's spend. (spec §6.2, §6.3)
- [ ] End-to-end regression test through the SAME recording function chat runs use (`recordSpend` with `routineId` null): create a task and run for a role with a small budget_usd, record spend for it, and `admitRunReservation` is denied `budget.role_exceeded`. This test must fail on the current master code. (ADR-005)
- [ ] Another role's spend and a run with no task are never counted toward this role; a non-UUID run id in spend_records does not raise.
- [ ] The concurrent-admission proof on the role axis (TASK-300's) still passes unmodified.
- [ ] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only; failures classified against the master baseline.
**Branch:** task/TASK-315-s5
**Started_At:** 2026-09-19T10:32:38Z
**Progress_Notes:**
- [2026-09-19T09:30:00Z] [ORCH] Filed from ORCH's own check of TASK-300 after autopilot approved it. TASK-301 now depends on this so the broker never wires an inert role axis.
- [2026-09-19T10:38:01Z] [SV:S5] Role axis recorded spend now derived run->task->role; regression tests added; existing c1 test rewritten to real run/task. Commit 6832849 on task/TASK-315-s5.

Standing Rule 5 (control can fail): traced the REAL chat path — recordSpend writes spend_records.run_id=run.runId; runs.task_id NOT NULL; tasks.role_id text NOT NULL (requireNonEmpty on every create) — so the JOIN run->task->role fires for real chat spend, and master's routine_id=roleId read summed plain chats (routineId null) to zero and could never deny. The three TASK-315 tests drive recordSpend with routineId null and assert budget.role_exceeded (would pass admitted:true on master = fail). ### TASK-316
**Title:** A failed chat run leaves the user in silence and hides the provider's reason -- surface both
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** S5
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.ts executeGeminiChatRun (throws "Gemini run was denied before it could answer." and drops `result.deniedReason`); packages/agent-providers/src/providers/gemini.ts (`deniedReason`); ADR-005 (a control or path that fails silently is a defect).
**Owned_Paths:** services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.ts, services/worker/src/chatRunDriver.test.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-315
**Description:** LIVE INCIDENT 2026-09-19 13:11: the user sent "hello" to BossMan in the mobile app and never got an answer. The run failed in 14 seconds with the generic "Gemini run was denied before it could answer."; the real cause (Gemini API HTTP 429, "Your prepayment credits are depleted") was in `result.deniedReason` and was thrown away, and NOTHING was written to the thread, so the app showed only the user's own message forever. Found only by hand-calling the API. Two fixes. (1) Carry the adapter's `deniedReason` into the thrown error and the run's failure_note (bounded length, no credentials, no request bodies). (2) When a chat run FAILS for any reason, insert a system-authored message into that thread so the user sees it, in plain words: the model provider rejected or could not complete the turn, the short reason, and that the owner has been notified/can retry. Do not include stack traces, keys or internal ids. This must not fire for runs that park for approval or human takeover (those have their own UI), only for terminal failures. Apply to both the Gemini and Claude sandbox lanes.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] A Gemini run denied with a deniedReason produces a failure_note containing that reason (bounded, no secrets).
- [ ] A terminal chat-run failure in either lane inserts exactly one visible system message into the thread; a run that parks (approval, takeover, secret request) does not.
- [ ] The message text is plain language and contains no stack trace, key, or internal id; a test asserts this against a reason string that contains a key-shaped token.
- [ ] A regression test drives the real driver with a fake adapter returning denied + reason and asserts both the failure_note and the thread message.
- [ ] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only; failures classified against the master baseline.
**Branch:** task/TASK-316-s5

### TASK-320
**Title:** Audit trail: refuse TRUNCATE at the database level, with a liveness test
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** infra/postgres/migrations/001_schema_v1.up.sql:47-56 (audit_events protected only by DO INSTEAD NOTHING rules); CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 4; docs/decisions/ADR-005-control-liveness.md; OpenBot comparison 2026-09-21 (its migration 0012 refuses TRUNCATE)
**Owned_Paths:** infra/postgres/migrations/032_audit_truncate_guard.up.sql, infra/postgres/migrations/032_audit_truncate_guard.down.sql, packages/audit/test/append-only.integration.test.ts
**Depends_On:** —
**Description:** audit_events is guarded only by two DO INSTEAD NOTHING rules. Postgres rules do not fire on TRUNCATE, so `TRUNCATE audit_events` empties the trail. Add a statement-level BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger that raises, in a new migration 032 with a down migration. Do NOT change the UPDATE/DELETE rules: about a dozen existing tests issue DELETE FROM audit_events for fixture cleanup and rely on it being a silent no-op (packages/db/src/runs.test.ts, secretRequests.test.ts, services/control-api chat.routes.test.ts and ports.test.ts, and others); converting those to raising triggers is a separate later task. Also confirm nothing in the repo or in scripts/test-isolated.ps1 runs TRUNCATE against audit_events or a CASCADE that reaches it (it would now raise). Write the migration rationale into your dossier; ORCH will turn it into a docs/decisions ADR (builders never own docs/**).
**Acceptance_Criteria:**

- [ ] The cap is per run: a second run of the same manager gets its own allowance; a run of a different manager is unaffected.
- [ ] A refused call is audited (project.fanout_capped) and returns an isError text the model can read; nothing is thrown out of the handler.

### TASK-326
**Title:** Watchdog: detect an unreachable database, not just open ports
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** critical
**Spec_References:** Incident 2026-09-22/23 (below); CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 3 (fail closed) and "Every mechanical control ships a liveness assertion"; docs/decisions/ADR-005-control-liveness.md; OpenBot (CopilotKit, MIT) comparison of 2026-09-21, five read-only passes; borrow the idea, never the code
**Owned_Paths:** infra/compose/service-watchdog.ps1, services/control-api/src/app.ts, services/control-api/src/openapi.ts, services/control-api/src/health.routes.test.ts, services/control-api/src/ports.ts, packages/db/src/database.ts, packages/db/src/index.ts
**Depends_On:** —
**Description:** Incident: at 17:13 SAST on 2026-09-22 Docker Desktop restarted and its engine stopped answering. Postgres refused every connection for about 29 hours, while infra/compose/service-watchdog.ps1 logged control-api, dashboard and worker "healthy" every two minutes, because it only checks that ports listen and the worker pid exists. Add a readiness route GET /health/ready to control-api that runs SELECT 1 through the app's own database pool with a short timeout (about 3 s) and returns 503 with a category (db_unreachable, db_timeout) on failure. Never put a connection string, host or credential in the response or the logs. Leave GET /health unchanged as the liveness route, and record in the dossier whether it touches the database today. The watchdog calls /health/ready on every tick. On failure it logs a distinct line "DATABASE UNREACHABLE (<category>)" and writes infra/compose/logs/db-unreachable.marker holding the first-seen time; on recovery it deletes the marker and logs the outage duration. It must not restart control-api or the worker in a loop because the database is down: restarting them does not fix the database. Docker recovery is opt-in only: when OIK_WATCHDOG_RESTART_DOCKER=1 (default off, because Docker Desktop on this machine also runs other projects' containers), after three consecutive failed ticks run `docker desktop restart` at most once per 30 minutes and log it.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] GET /health/ready returns 200 when the database answers and 503 with a category when it does not: a real-Postgres test for 200 and a test pointed at a closed port for 503; the response carries no connection details.
- [ ] ADR-005 liveness: the watchdog gains a -SelfTest switch that points it at a stub returning 503 and asserts the DATABASE UNREACHABLE line and the marker are produced, then that a 200 clears the marker. Paste the self-test output into Test_Evidence. It must fail if the readiness call is removed from the tick.
- [ ] On database failure the watchdog never restart-loops control-api or the worker. A Docker restart happens only with the env flag set, is rate-limited to once per 30 minutes, and is logged.
- [ ] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only; every non-own-package failure classified against the master baseline in Test_Evidence.

### TASK-327
**Title:** Harden role-message delivery: isolate failures, cap attempts, tell the sender
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** high
**Spec_References:** OpenBot comparison (agents/handoff-delivery.ts: per-hop lease, attempt cap, in-voice notice to the asker); services/worker/src/roleMessageDelivery.ts; OpenBot (CopilotKit, MIT) comparison of 2026-09-21, five read-only passes; borrow the idea, never the code
**Owned_Paths:** services/worker/src/roleMessageDelivery.ts, services/worker/src/roleMessageDelivery.test.ts, packages/db/src/roleMessages.ts, packages/db/src/roleMessages.test.ts, packages/db/src/index.ts, infra/postgres/migrations/035_role_message_delivery_attempts.up.sql, infra/postgres/migrations/035_role_message_delivery_attempts.down.sql
**Depends_On:** TASK-333, TASK-342
**Description:** REPORTED by the OpenBot pass, verify each point against the code first: deliverPendingRoleMessages (roleMessageDelivery.ts, about lines 171-173) has no per-row error handling, so one throwing row aborts the rest of the tick; it enqueues the run first and marks the message read last, so a crash between the two delivers twice (documented around lines 34-41); a message to an inactive recipient stays unread and is retried every minute forever; and the sender is never told. Fix: isolate each row; add delivery_attempts and last_delivery_error (a category, never message content or secrets) in migration 035; claim each row atomically before enqueueing, so a second tick or worker cannot deliver it twice; after five failed attempts, or immediately when the recipient role is not active, mark the message terminally failed and insert exactly one visible system message into the SENDER's thread naming the recipient and the reason. Keep the existing no-same-turn-reply semantics.
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] A poison row (a recipient whose delivery throws) does not stop the other rows in the same tick.
- [ ] Attempts are capped at five, then the message is terminal with exactly one visible notice in the sender's thread; an inactive recipient goes terminal immediately with one notice.
- [ ] Two concurrent delivery ticks deliver one message exactly once (real Postgres).
- [ ] ADR-005 liveness: a test keyed on the terminal-failure audit event or notice fails if the cap or the notice is removed.
- [ ] Migration 035 is idempotent (up, down, up).
- [ ] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only; every non-own-package failure classified against the master baseline in Test_Evidence.

### TASK-328
**Title:** Handoff hop-depth cap and idempotent role-message send
**Status:** done
**Assigned_To:** CX9
**Priority:** medium
**Spec_References:** OpenBot comparison (agents/handoff.ts: depth carried in a signed run assertion, fan-out counted under an advisory lock, envelope-hash idempotency); specs/OIKONOMOS_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_v1.0.md section 6.4; OpenBot (CopilotKit, MIT) comparison of 2026-09-21, five read-only passes; borrow the idea, never the code
**Owned_Paths:** packages/db/src/roleMessages.ts, packages/db/src/roleMessages.test.ts, packages/db/src/index.ts, services/worker/src/roleMessageDelivery.ts, services/worker/src/roleMessageDelivery.test.ts, infra/postgres/migrations/036_role_message_depth_dedupe.up.sql, infra/postgres/migrations/036_role_message_depth_dedupe.down.sql, services/worker/src/projectTools.ts, services/worker/src/projectTools.test.ts, services/worker/src/workspaceMcpServer.ts, services/worker/src/workspaceMcpServer.test.ts, services/worker/src/geminiToolExecutors.ts, services/worker/src/geminiToolExecutors.test.ts, services/workspace/src/mailbox.ts, services/workspace/src/mailbox.test.ts, services/control-api/src/chat.routes.test.ts
**Depends_On:** TASK-327, TASK-340
**Description:** Nothing caps how deep a chain of bot-to-bot handoffs can go: A to B to C to A is bounded only by spend. And an identical resend within one run creates a second message and a second run. Add hop_depth (default 0) and dedupe_key to role_messages (migration 036). sendRoleMessage takes an optional sourceRunId. Depth is the depth of the message that started the source run (runs.requested_by = "role-message:<id>") plus one, else 0. Refuse at depth >= OIK_HANDOFF_MAX_DEPTH (default 4) with a sentence the model can read: isError text in the Claude MCP lanes, tool-result text in the Gemini lane. The dedupe key is a SHA-256 of (from role, to role, handoff kind, body, factRef, sourceRunId), unique among the source run's messages; an identical second send returns "already sent" and creates no row and no run. Audit both refusals with a category only. Every caller in both lanes passes its run id: projectTools.ts, workspaceMcpServer.ts (send_to_role) and geminiToolExecutors.ts (send_to_role).
**Acceptance_Criteria:**
- [ ] A real-Postgres A to B to C to A chain is refused at the cap, and depth provably travels source run to message to delivered run.
- [ ] An identical second send in the same run creates no second row and no second run; the same body in a different run is allowed.
- [ ] Both lanes pass the run id: one test through the Claude MCP path and one through the Gemini executor.
- [ ] ADR-005 liveness: tests keyed on the depth_capped and duplicate audit events fail if either check is removed.
- [ ] Migration 036 is idempotent (up, down, up).
- [ ] Full recursive suite via scripts/test-isolated.ps1 only; every non-own-package failure classified against the master baseline in Test_Evidence.

**Description:** These test bugs have been labelled "baseline" in every review. Fix them at the source. (a) The last test in packages/db/src/spendReservations.test.ts (~L248) records $100 of spend under a bare randomUUID() runId that its cleanup never deletes. Every run leaks $100 into spend_records, and the platform budget (R350, about $18.92) then fails every later budget check in a full `pnpm -r` run with budget.platform_exceeded. Track that runId in spendRunIds, or use the file's run() helper. (e) Three real-pg-boss tests in services/worker/src/roleMessageDelivery.ts (~L414, 442, 469) call deliverPendingRoleMessages without withPgBossQueueLock. A parallel purge of worker.run-execution in routineJob.test.ts or workerJobQueue.test.ts can delete the queue between its create and send, giving "Queue worker.run-execution does not exist". Wrap them in withPgBossQueueLock. (f) The same file's afterAll (~L337) deletes threads before thread_members, which violates thread_members_thread_id_fkey; delete thread_members first. (g) Classify and fix workspaceTools.test.ts "requires real approvals for T3 create_bot and E6-gated retire_bot" (TASK-285), which gets deny where it expects allow. It may be downstream of the email.send drift that TASK-338 F4 fixes; if so, say so and don't change it. Change nothing outside Owned_Paths.
